questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Point of Intersection of a Circle and a Radial Line
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14040379/assets/7a3c82568cfaf845708a9dcee79a3ac2e0e9d2131776fd1c7daa1c598473f3b3.png)

The polar curve $r=10$ and the ray $\theta =\frac{7\pi }{6}$ intersect at the point $P,$ as shown above. What are the Cartesian coordinates of $P?$
questions.worked_solution:
The polar coordinates of $P$ are $(r,\theta )=(10,\frac{7\pi }{6}).$ We can convert the polar coordinates of $P$ to Cartesian coordinates, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =10\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{6}) \\  & =10\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\  & =-5\sqrt{3} \\ y & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =10\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{6}) \\  & =10\cdot (-\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =-5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian coordinates of $P$ are $(-5\sqrt{3},-5).$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Polar Equation of a Radial Line That Passes Through a Given Point
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14040379/assets/5507850932bb4061cd19cdbffa18aacf2b235293e643170ee78c4326a96e050d.png)

Given that the ray above passes through the point with Cartesian coordinates $(9,-3\sqrt{3})$, find the polar equation of the ray.
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the reference angle associated with the point:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{R} & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡|\frac{y}{x}| \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡|\frac{-3\sqrt{3}}{9}| \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the ray lies in the fourth quadrant. So, we find the angle in the fourth quadrant that has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{6},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta  & =2\pi -{\theta }_{R} \\  & =2\pi -\frac{\pi }{6} \\  & =\frac{11\pi }{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the polar equation of the ray is 

$$
\theta =\frac{11\pi }{6}.
$$

Find the polar equation of the ray shown above. Assume that the polar angle is in the range $[0,2\pi ).$

The polar equation is $\theta =$
{{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
The counterclockwise angle that the ray makes with the positive $x$-axis is

$$
\pi -\frac{\pi }{4}=\frac{3\pi }{4}.
$$

Therefore, the polar equation of the ray is $\theta =\frac{3\pi }{4}.$
